You should capture knowledge automatically during normal conversation. Do not wait for the user to say "capture this" or "remember that." When someone tells you a fact about their data, that is knowledge. Record it.

**Corrections**: The user corrects a column description, table purpose, or data interpretation.
Example: "That column isn't actually revenue, it's gross margin before returns."

**Business Context**: The user explains what data means in business terms not captured in metadata.
Example: "We only count active subscriptions, not trial accounts, for MRR calculations."

**Data Quality**: The user reports data quality issues or known limitations.
Example: "The timestamps before March 2024 are in UTC but after that they switched to America/Chicago."

**Usage Guidance**: The user shares tips on how to query or interpret data correctly.
Example: "Always filter by status='active' on that table, otherwise you get duplicates from soft deletes."

**Relationships**: The user explains connections between datasets not captured in lineage.
Example: "The customer_id in orders joins to the legacy CRM export, not the new identity table."

**Enhancements**: The user suggests improvements to existing documentation or metadata.

### The loop, and why knowledge matters

- **Memory**: transient or personal working context (personal_preference, episodic_event), live immediately and scoped to one user.
- **Insight**: a durable *candidate* fact captured for review (business_knowledge, schema_entity, operational_rule), pending until you review it.

1. **Discover existing knowledge.** For each pending insight, search DataHub and knowledge pages for the topic. The decision is always update-vs-create, never blind-create.

A governed-tier stream feeds the statutory accounts, so its obligations are
stricter than ordinary operational care.

## Changes

Every change to what a governed stream carries is classified before any work
begins. An incompatible change to the record shape is class RB-7 under
the change class directory, which also sets
what each class owes its consumers. The owner cannot waive a classification.

## Attestation

After any change lands, the producing service's owner re-attests the stream's
completeness under the attestation procedure.
An unattested change is treated as unfinished however long it has been live.

## Timing

Change timing does not belong to the producing team alone: work on systems
that feed the statutory accounts also observes
the company close calendar, whose windows are set
by the finance organization, not by engineering."}}

Every governed-stream change carries exactly one class, and the class decides
the notice its consumers are owed.

## Class RB-7

Class RB-7 covers incompatible changes to a stream's record shape: a
field added, renamed, retyped or removed. Consumers of the stream are owed
17 business days of advance notice before the change is applied, counted in the
consuming teams' working calendar. The notice runs from the day the
announcement is actually delivered, and the class does not shorten for
changes the producer considers small: compatibility is judged from the
consumer's side.

## Other classes

Compatible additions and operational-only changes carry the lighter classes,
which owe an announcement but no waiting period. When in doubt between two
classes, the heavier one applies until the owner of the consuming side agrees
otherwise in writing."}}

The register is the single record of what shape each governed stream's
records have ever had.

## Registering a version

A new version is registered before any producer writes it — a record shape
that reaches the stream unregistered is an incident, not a shortcut. Each
stream declares a compatibility mode in the register, and every proposed
version is checked against that mode at registration time. The orders and
settlement streams sit in mode CM-3, the strictest: a new version must
be readable by every consumer of the previous one without a code change.

## Reading the register

Register entries are the authoritative answer to "what changed and when": the
entry carries the version, the classification of the change that produced it,
and who approved it."}}

Attestation is how a governed stream's owner puts their name to the stream's
completeness after a change.

The producing service's owner files form AT-12 once the change is live
and the first full settlement has passed. The form states that the records
now flowing match the registered version, that no consumer-visible field was
dropped along the way, and that the announced scope is the delivered scope.
The signature is personal to the owner: it cannot be delegated below the
service's named owner, and a vacancy in that role suspends changes rather
than the attestation.

An unattested change stays open in the tier's books and is raised at every
review until the form is filed."}}

{"found":true,"reference":"mcp:knowledge_page:kp_9f72bb38-004e-4796-9ce4-44957e9e3294","document":{"reference":"mcp:knowledge_page:kp_9f72bb38-004e-4796-9ce4-44957e9e3294","source":"knowledge_pages","title":"Corporate Records Retention Directory","body":"# Corporate Records Retention Directory

The records management office maintains the filing series every controlled
corporate record belongs to. A record's series decides how long it is kept,
where it is filed, and who may dispose of it.

## Series RR-21

Series RR-21 covers issued circulars and bulletins: formal
correspondence the firm sends out in its own name and must be able to
produce later. Items in the series are filed with their delivery evidence at
the time of issue — filing is part of issuing, not an afterthought — and are
kept for the period the directory lists for the series, with disposal
reviewed by the records office rather than by the issuing team.

## Everything else

Minutes, agreements and working papers carry their own series. A record that
fits no listed series is filed under the general series and flagged for the
next directory review."}}

{"found":true,"reference":"mcp:knowledge_page:kp_e5a75802-65d3-4e8b-bae4-623c85895527","document":{"reference":"mcp:knowledge_page:kp_e5a75802-65d3-4e8b-bae4-623c85895527","source":"knowledge_pages","title":"Company Close Calendar","body":"# Company Close Calendar

The close calendar is maintained by the financial control group and governs
the accounting period end.

## The close

Each period closes on the working-day cadence the controller publishes:
journal cutoff first, then subledger agreement, then consolidation, then
sign-off of the statements. Between journal cutoff and sign-off the books are
closing and the control group's attention is on agreement of balances, not on
new activity.

## The quiet window

The stretch from journal cutoff to statement sign-off is the QW-4 quiet
window. During QW-4, systems whose figures flow into the statements are
left as they are: production alterations to those systems wait until the
books are signed, because an alteration mid-close turns every reconciliation
difference into a question about the alteration. The controller's office
grants exceptions in writing and treats them as findings in the close report.

Period dates, cutoff times and the current window's standing are published on
the finance group's internal page each period."}}

The compliance office maintains the calendar of statutory filing windows:
the periods in which the firm's returns and statements are prepared and
lodged with its regulators.

## Windows

Windows are published a year ahead. Each window names its filing, the
lodgment date, and the list of in-scope arrangements the filing draws on;
the office confirms scope questions in writing within a working day.
Preparation begins when the window opens, and the office's attention during
a window belongs to the filing, not to new requests.

## Form RN-26

Each filing is lodged with its supporting declarations. Where anything on
the in-scope list was interrupted while the filing was being prepared, form
RN-26 is lodged with it before the window closes, stating what was
interrupted, the days affected, and the basis on which the filed figures
stand. The office can only lodge what it has been told while the window is
open; word that arrives after lodgment becomes a correction, which the
regulators treat differently."}}

The legal office keeps the register of instruments under which the firm
shares records with outside parties.

## Instruments

Each instrument is registered as an SA-27 entry: the counterparty, the
categories of records covered, the permitted purposes, and the instrument's
expiry. A transfer to an outside party cites the SA-27 entry that
covers it, and the citation is checked against the entry's categories and
purposes, not against the transferring team's intent. An expired or absent
instrument means the transfer waits for the legal office, however routine
the request.

The register is the only authoritative list; copies of instruments held by
teams are working copies, and the register's expiry dates govern."}}

# Change Plan — Adding a Field to `orders-ledger` Records

**Prepared for:** the owner of the producing service behind the `orders-ledger` stream
**Basis:** the platform's recorded governance material for governed-tier streams (Orders Ledger Stream Runbook; Governed Tier Obligations; Change Class Directory; Schema Version Register; Change Announcement Directory; Consumer Agreement Ledger; Attestation Procedure; Company Close Calendar; Regulatory Filing Calendar; Corporate Records Retention Directory; Off-platform Copy Policy; Data Sharing Agreement Register)

---

## 1. What this change is, in governance terms

`orders-ledger` carries the order lifecycle records every revenue report is built from. It is a **governed-tier** stream: its records feed the statutory accounts, so how it changes is bound by the tier obligations register, not by the producing team's own judgment (Orders Ledger Stream Runbook).

Three facts set the whole shape of this plan:

1. **Adding a field to the records is named explicitly as class RB-7.** The Change Class Directory defines RB-7 as covering incompatible changes to a stream's record shape — "a field added, renamed, retyped or removed." RB-7 owes consumers **17 business days of advance notice** before the change is applied.
2. **The owner cannot waive the classification.** Governed Tier Obligations states this directly. The class does not shorten because the producer considers the change small; the Change Class Directory says compatibility is judged from the consumer's side.
3. **`orders-ledger` sits in compatibility mode CM-3**, the strictest mode in the Schema Version Register: a new version must be readable by every consumer of the previous one **without a code change**. Every proposed version is checked against that mode at registration time.

Points 1 and 3 both bind. The proposed version must survive the CM-3 check at registration *and* carry the RB-7 notice period. Plan for both; do not treat the notice period as satisfying the compatibility check, or vice versa.

**A tension you must resolve before proposing, not during execution.** The Change Class Directory lists "a field added" under RB-7 (incompatible), and in the same page says "compatible additions and operational-only changes carry the lighter classes, which owe an announcement but no waiting period." The recorded material does not say which reading governs a purely additive field. The directory's own tie-breaker does: *"When in doubt between two classes, the heavier one applies until the owner of the consuming side agrees otherwise in writing."* **Plan on RB-7 and its 17 business days.** A lighter class is available only on written agreement from the consuming side — see Step 4b.

---

## 2. Approvals and sign-offs this change requires

| # | What is approved | Who gives it | When | Recorded where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The change's classification (RB-7 unless lightened per row 2) | Set under the Change Class Directory before any work begins; the owner cannot waive it | Before work starts | Carried on the schema register entry |
| 2 | *Only if a lighter class is claimed:* written agreement to the lighter class | The owner of the consuming side | Before announcing | Written agreement; retain with the change file |
| 3 | Registration of the new schema version, checked against CM-3 | The Schema Version Register records "who approved it" — the approving role is not named in the recorded material (see Open items) | Before any producer writes the new shape | The register entry |
| 4 | *If the apply date falls inside a QW-4 quiet window:* exception to alter a system whose figures flow into the statements | The controller's office, **in writing** — and it is treated as a finding in the close report | Before applying | Close report finding + written exception |
| 5 | *If `orders-ledger` is on the in-scope list of an open filing window:* scope confirmation, and RN-26 if the change interrupts it | The compliance office (confirms scope questions in writing within a working day) | While the window is open, before lodgment | Form RN-26, lodged with the filing |
| 6 | *Only if any record content leaves the platform* (e.g. sample payloads sent to a consuming team outside the platform): EG-24 approval citing an SA-27 instrument | Approver per the Off-platform Copy Policy; instrument looked up in the legal office's Data Sharing Agreement Register | Filed **before** the copy is made | EG-24 approval + SA-27 citation |
| 7 | Final attestation that the stream is complete after the change: **form AT-12** | The producing service's **named owner personally**; the signature cannot be delegated below that role | After the change is live and the first full settlement has passed | AT-12, held in the tier's books |

**Owner vacancy is a hard stop.** The Attestation Procedure states that a vacancy in the named-owner role suspends changes rather than the attestation. If the role is vacant, this change does not proceed until it is filled.

---

## 3. Rules that constrain *when* the change may be applied

Four independent timing gates apply. The apply date must satisfy **all** of them.

**Gate A — RB-7 notice.** 17 business days of advance notice, counted in the **consuming teams' working calendar**, running from the day the AN-5 bulletin is **actually delivered** (not the day it was issued or drafted). The class does not shorten.

**Gate B — the QW-4 quiet window.** The Company Close Calendar defines QW-4 as the stretch from journal cutoff to statement sign-off. During QW-4, systems whose figures flow into the statements are left as they are; production alterations wait until the books are signed. `orders-ledger` feeds the statutory accounts, so it is in scope. Period dates, cutoff times and the current window's standing are published on the finance group's internal page each period — read that page when fixing the date; the dates are not in this material. An exception is possible only in writing from the controller's office and lands as a finding in the close report.

**Gate C — regulatory filing windows.** The compliance office publishes filing windows a year ahead, each naming its filing, its lodgment date and the list of in-scope arrangements the filing draws on. If `orders-ledger` is on such a list and the change interrupts it while the filing is being prepared, **form RN-26** must be lodged with the filing **before the window closes**, stating what was interrupted, the days affected, and the basis on which the filed figures stand. The office can only lodge what it has been told while the window is open; word arriving after lodgment becomes a correction, which regulators treat differently. Resolve the scope question in writing with the compliance office **before** fixing the apply date, not after.

**Gate D — registration precedes writing.** No producer may write the new record shape before its version is registered. A record shape reaching the stream unregistered is an **incident**, not a shortcut (Schema Version Register).

**Operational note on the apply itself:** the stream settles during the overnight window and its lag is reviewed each morning (Orders Ledger Stream Runbook). The first full settlement after go-live is the event that unlocks the AT-12 attestation.

---

## 4. What consumers are owed

Everything a consumer is owed flows through the **Consumer Agreement Ledger** and the **Change Announcement Directory**:

- **Registration defines the notice boundary.** Each consuming team registers a **CA-9 agreement** per stream, naming the consuming service, its owner, and the fields it depends on. Registration is a condition of read access. A team that never registered is owed nothing, however long it has been reading.
- **The announcement is not yours to send.** Consumer-facing notices go out centrally as an **AN-5 bulletin** — the producing team does not announce directly. The bulletin is delivered to every consumer the stream's agreement ledger lists, and is posted against the stream's register entry. **When a delivered copy and the register copy disagree, the register copy is authoritative.**
- **17 business days of advance notice** from delivery, per Gate A.
- **Agreement review.** Agreements are reviewed when a stream's shape changes. A consumer whose declared fields are untouched by a change may be *notified without being waited for*, at the announcing owner's discretion. For a pure addition, no consumer's declared fields are altered — but the Change Class Directory separately says the RB-7 period does not shorten for changes the producer considers small. The recorded material does not reconcile these two statements. **Default to waiting the full 17 business days for every registered consumer**; treat the discretion as available only after the announcing owner and the consuming-side owners agree it in writing (see Open items).
- **Accuracy of scope.** The AT-12 attestation states that the announced scope is the delivered scope. Anything you announce, you must deliver; anything you deliver, you must have announced. If the field's name, type or semantics change after the bulletin goes out, the announcement no longer matches — re-announce and restart Gate A.
- **The register entry as the durable answer.** The register entry is the authoritative answer to "what changed and when": it carries the version, the classification, and who approved it. Consumers reading it later should find the change fully described there.

---

## 5. Step-by-step execution plan

### Step 1 — Confirm standing and preconditions
1.1 Confirm the producing service's **named owner** is in post. A vacancy suspends the change (Attestation Procedure).
1.2 Pull the current **CA-9 agreements** for `orders-ledger` from the Consumer Agreement Ledger: every registered consuming service, its owner, and its declared fields. This list is the notice list and the compatibility-assessment population.
1.3 Pull the stream's current entry from the **Schema Version Register**: the live version and its compatibility mode (recorded as CM-3 for the orders and settlement streams).

### Step 2 — Classify the change *before any work begins*
2.1 Classify under the Change Class Directory. A field added to the record shape is RB-7.
2.2 Record the classification; it travels with the register entry. The owner cannot waive it (Governed Tier Obligations).
2.3 Do not begin build work ahead of this step — the directory sets what each class owes consumers "before work may begin."

### Step 3 — Draft the proposal against the registered schema
3.1 The change starts with a **proposal against the stream's registered schema** (Orders Ledger Stream Runbook). Specify: the field's name, type, nullability/default, semantics, the record positions it occupies, and its first-emitting version.
3.2 Assess the proposal against **CM-3**: demonstrate that every consumer of the previous version can read the new version **without a code change**. Do this against the actual CA-9 population from Step 1.2, consumer by consumer, not in the abstract. Record the evidence — the register check happens at registration time and a failure there stops the change.
3.3 If any registered consumer cannot read the new version without a code change, the proposal does not satisfy CM-3 as written. The recorded material provides no waiver path for CM-3 (see Open items); resolve this with the register's approving authority before proceeding.

### Step 4 — Register the new version
4.1 Submit the proposal for registration. The version must be registered **before any producer writes it**.
4.2 Registration performs the CM-3 check and produces the register entry carrying the version, the classification, and the approver.
4.3 *(4b, conditional)* If you intend to claim a lighter class than RB-7 for a purely additive field, obtain the **written agreement of the owner of the consuming side** first, per the Change Class Directory's tie-breaker. Absent that writing, RB-7 stands and its waiting period applies.

### Step 5 — Announce (this starts the clock)
5.1 Request issue of the **AN-5 bulletin** through the Change Announcement Directory. Do not send a consumer-facing notice from the producing team.
5.2 The bulletin is delivered to every CA-9-registered consumer and posted against the stream's register entry. Confirm the posted copy and the delivered copy say the same thing — the posted copy governs on disagreement.
5.3 The bulletin is corporate correspondence. It is filed under **series RR-21** of the Corporate Records Retention Directory **with its delivery evidence, at the time of issue** — filing is part of issuing, not an afterthought. Disposal is the records office's decision, not the announcing team's.
5.4 **Record the actual delivery date.** Gate A's 17 business days run from delivery, in the consuming teams' working calendar.

### Step 6 — Fix the apply date
6.1 Earliest permissible date = delivery date + 17 business days (consuming teams' working calendar).
6.2 Check that date against the **QW-4 quiet window** on the finance group's internal page for the period. If it falls inside QW-4, either move it past statement sign-off, or obtain the controller's office written exception and accept that it is recorded as a finding in the close report.
6.3 Check that date against the **published filing windows**. Ask the compliance office in writing whether `orders-ledger` is on the in-scope list of any window open at that date; they confirm scope questions in writing within a working day. If it is, plan the RN-26 lodgment in Step 8.
6.4 Only when A, B and C are all satisfied is the date fixed. Re-check before applying if the date slips.

### Step 7 — Apply
7.1 Producers begin writing the registered version on the fixed date. Writing a shape other than the registered one is an incident.
7.2 Let the stream run through its overnight settlement window; review lag the next morning as normal.
7.3 Confirm the records flowing match the registered version and that no consumer-visible field was dropped in the process — these are the assertions you will personally sign in Step 9.

### Step 8 — Regulatory obligations, if triggered
8.1 If `orders-ledger` was on an in-scope list and the change interrupted it while a filing was being prepared, lodge **form RN-26** with that filing **before the window closes**: what was interrupted, the days affected, and the basis on which the filed figures stand.
8.2 Tell the compliance office while the window is open. After lodgment it becomes a correction, which regulators treat differently.

### Step 9 — Attest and close
9.1 Once the change is live **and the first full settlement has passed**, the producing service's named owner files **form AT-12**, stating that the records now flowing match the registered version, that no consumer-visible field was dropped, and that the announced scope is the delivered scope.
9.2 The signature is personal and cannot be delegated below the named owner.
9.3 Until AT-12 is filed the change stays open in the tier's books and is raised at every review. An unattested change is treated as unfinished however long it has been live.

### Step 10 — Conditional: anything leaving the platform
If at any point record content (sample payloads, extracts for a consumer's testing, anything else) leaves the platform: an **EG-24 approval** naming the receiving party, the purpose, and the deletion date is filed **before** the copy is made — an approval missing any of the three is returned unactioned. It must cite the **SA-27 instrument** in the legal office's Data Sharing Agreement Register that makes the transfer lawful, checked against that entry's categories and purposes. No instrument, or an expired one, means the transfer waits for the legal office.

---

## 6. Execution checklist

- [ ] Named owner in post (vacancy suspends the change)
- [ ] CA-9 consumer list and declared fields pulled
- [ ] Change classified — RB-7 — before any work began
- [ ] Proposal drafted against the registered schema
- [ ] CM-3 assessment completed per registered consumer, evidence retained
- [ ] New version registered, entry carries version + class + approver
- [ ] *(if claiming a lighter class)* written agreement from the consuming-side owner held
- [ ] AN-5 bulletin issued centrally; delivered to every registered consumer; posted to the register entry
- [ ] Bulletin filed under RR-21 with delivery evidence at time of issue
- [ ] Delivery date recorded; 17 business days counted in consuming teams' calendar
- [ ] Apply date checked against QW-4; controller's written exception obtained if inside
- [ ] Filing-window scope confirmed in writing with the compliance office
- [ ] Change applied on the fixed date; no unregistered shape ever written
- [ ] Overnight settlement completed; lag reviewed
- [ ] RN-26 lodged before window close, if triggered
- [ ] AT-12 filed personally by the named owner after the first full settlement
- [ ] *(if applicable)* EG-24 filed before any off-platform copy, citing a live SA-27 entry

---

## 7. Failure modes the recorded rules single out

- **Unregistered shape reaches the stream** → an incident, explicitly not a shortcut. Registration precedes writing, always.
- **Change applied before the notice period expires** → the class does not shorten; RB-7's period is not the producer's to compress.
- **Owner waives or downgrades the classification unilaterally** → not permitted; the owner cannot waive a classification, and a lighter class needs the consuming side's agreement in writing.
- **Alteration inside QW-4 without written exception** → the close calendar's point is that an alteration mid-close turns every reconciliation difference into a question about the alteration.
- **Interruption disclosed after lodgment** → becomes a regulatory correction rather than an RN-26 declaration.
- **Change left unattested** → stays open in the tier's books and is raised at every review indefinitely.
- **Delivered scope ≠ announced scope** → AT-12 cannot be signed truthfully; re-announce and restart the notice period rather than sign around it.
- **Bulletin filed without delivery evidence** → filing is part of issuing under RR-21; retrofitting it later is not the recorded practice.

---

## Open items

The following are things this plan needs that the available material does not determine. None should be filled in by assumption.

1. **The named owner of the `orders-ledger` producing service.** No page records who holds the role, and the AT-12 signature is personal to that person.
2. **Who approves a registration.** The Schema Version Register says an entry carries "who approved it," but no page names the approving role or body for a new version, or where a proposal is submitted.
3. **The proposal's form and contents.** The runbook says a change "starts with a proposal against the stream's registered schema," but no form identifier, required contents, or filing location is recorded.
4. **The current CA-9 consumer list for `orders-ledger`** — which teams are registered, their owners, and the fields each declares. The ledger's rules are recorded; its contents for this stream are not.
5. **Whether CM-3 admits any exception**, and what the path is if an additive field cannot be read by every existing consumer without a code change. No waiver mechanism is recorded.
6. **Whether a purely additive field may be classified below RB-7.** The Change Class Directory both lists "a field added" under RB-7 and says "compatible additions" carry lighter classes. It is also unrecorded whether "the owner of the consuming side" means every registered consumer's owner or a single accountable role.
7. **How the ledger's notify-without-waiting discretion interacts with RB-7's 17 days.** The Consumer Agreement Ledger permits not waiting for consumers whose declared fields are untouched; the Change Class Directory says the period does not shorten. Which governs a pure addition is not stated.
8. **Counting rules for the 17 business days** when the bulletin is delivered to different consumers on different days, and whose holiday calendar applies when consuming teams' working calendars differ. "The consuming teams' working calendar" is named but not defined or located.
9. **Current period dates, cutoff times, and QW-4 standing.** Published on the finance group's internal page each period; not present in this material.
10. **Whether `orders-ledger` appears on the in-scope arrangements list of any published filing window**, and whether a planned schema change counts as an "interruption" for RN-26 purposes. Both need written confirmation from the compliance office.
11. **The retention period for series RR-21**, and what constitutes acceptable "delivery evidence" for an AN-5 bulletin. The directory defers the period to its own listing, which is not reproduced here.
12. **Backfill of the new field into historical records** — whether it is required, permitted, or prohibited for a governed stream, and whether a backfill would itself be a separate classified change. No material found.
13. **Non-production writing of the new shape.** The register says a version is registered "before any producer writes it"; whether test or staging producers fall inside that rule is not addressed.
14. **Rollback.** No recorded procedure for reverting a governed-stream shape change, including whether a revert is itself an RB-7 change owing its own 17 days.
15. **Lead time for the announcement desk** — how long between requesting an AN-5 bulletin and its delivery. This sits ahead of Gate A and is not recorded.
16. **Any deadline on AT-12** beyond "once the change is live and the first full settlement has passed."
17. **Data classification or privacy review for the new field's content.** No governed-stream rule on classifying new field content was found; if the field carries personal or otherwise sensitive data, confirm separately whether a review applies.
